newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end weaker amid light local selling.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end weaker amid light local selling.

text.p: Frozen concentrated orange juice futures settled a thinly-traded session lower amid local selling and a dearth of buying interest, market sources said.

"The locals went home long last night and sold on the open," an analyst said. She said stops were triggered around 76.00 cents in May, sending the contract to the low of 75.30. A lack of bids held prices near the lows throughout the day, she added.
Activity remained thin, with many players attending the National Juice Processors' Association meeting in Arizona. The meeting began today.
Volume was estimated at a slim 1,500 lots compared with Wednesday's official 2,387 lots.
Resistance remained between 77.00 and 78.00 cents basis the May contract, and support at 74.00 cents.
The spot month closed 1.00 lower to 75.70, having traded from 76.90 to 75.30 cents. July ended down 0.65 at 78.55, while the outer contracts finished 0.35 to 0.65 lower.
Open interest in May fell 564 lots to 9,568 lots while July gained 102 lots to 10,621 lots, as of Tuesday's close.

A dearth of fundamental news should keep trade dull, analysts said. Following last week's U.S. Department of Agriculture's Florida crop estimate, players await the Brazilian crop estimate released May 20.
Also, the Florida Citrus Processors' Association will release its weekly movement data later today.
